headline: Curtiss-Wright posts broad-based growth with margin gains
summary_short: Curtiss-Wright's Q1 2026 sales rose 13% y/y to $914M (12% organic) with operating margin up 150bp to 17.5%, and diluted EPS grew 29% to $3.46 as new orders climbed 16% to $1.2B, lifting backlog to $4.3B.
summary_long: Q1 2026 sales rose 13% y/y to $914M (12% organic, 1% FX), with growth across every segment: Naval & Power +21%, Aerospace & Industrial +12%, Defense Electronics +5%. Operating margin expanded 150bp to 17.5% on favorable absorption from higher volume and favorable mix in Defense Electronics and Naval & Power. Net income rose 26% to $128M ($3.46 diluted EPS). New orders climbed 16% y/y to $1.2B on naval, nuclear, and ground-defense demand, lifting backlog to $4.3B. Operating cash outflow narrowed to $5.7M from $38.8M on higher cash earnings and working-capital improvement. Cash fell to $343M after $14M of buybacks; total debt held flat at $958M.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based and 12% organic across all three segments: Naval & Power +21% on submarine production timing and nuclear demand, Aerospace & Industrial +12% on aerospace/general-industrial demand, Defense Electronics +5% on embedded computing and avionics.
Grew roughly in line with the 13% sales increase; the release discusses operating margin expansion but does not separately break out gross margin drivers.

Operating margin expanded 150bp to 17.5% primarily on favorable absorption from higher sales across all segments, with Defense Electronics and Naval & Power also benefiting from favorable product mix.
Rose 26% to $128M on higher operating income; the effective tax rate also improved slightly to 18.7% from 19.0% on stock-based compensation tax benefits.
Tracks the 26% net income gain plus a modestly lower diluted share count (37.058M vs 37.851M y/y) from continued buybacks.
Follows the same operating-income drivers — higher sales, favorable absorption and mix — plus depreciation and amortization add-back.
Cash used in operations narrowed to $5.7M from $38.8M, primarily due to higher cash earnings and improved working capital.
Cash rose $117M y/y to $343M mainly because the prior-year quarter included a $90M debt principal repayment and other financing outflows that didn't recur this year.
Held essentially flat at $958M y/y; the quarter's only revolver activity was drawn and repaid in full within the period.

Broad-based segment growth drove double-digit sales, operating income, and net income gains; new orders rose 16% to $1.2B, lifting backlog to $4.3B. No new guidance was issued in this quarterly filing.
